mission-board.lede: The board is heavy on finished work and light on contact with anyone outside the system. Nearly every live thread has a made thing sitting at ready — teardowns, listing content, an offer, a studio — and almost none of them carry a recorded response from a buyer, a client or an audience.
mission-board.next_move: Pick the single finished asset closest to a real person and send it.
mission-board.caveats: Stage and status are inferred from records the system wrote about itself, so a thread can read as shipped while nothing has left the building. Threads with no recorded activity in this window are shown as last left, not as currently true. A meaningful share of the files this sweep catalogued no longer exist on disk, so the artifact picture is a snapshot of what was claimed, not of what survives.
mission-board.operator_read: Production is not the bottleneck — the work is built and it isn't being sent.

linkedin-launch.lede: The launch lane is the one thing moving right now: a fresh brand teardown in flight with its assets already generated. It is the execution arm of the offer the rest of the board has been preparing.
linkedin-launch.next_move: Finish the teardown in flight and put it in front of the brand it profiles.
linkedin-launch.caveats: The record captures work being made, not delivered — no reply, booked call or outcome is attached to anything in this lane yet.
linkedin-launch.operator_read: Live and producing; the gap is between publishing a teardown and someone answering it.

teardown-1-fresh.lede: Three named-brand teardowns are finished at the standard the offer is meant to demonstrate — each with its own analysis, outreach message and adversarial pass, each rendered into shareable form. This is the proof asset the campaign rests on.
teardown-1-fresh.next_move: Send the finished teardowns to the brands they analyze.
teardown-1-fresh.caveats: Earlier teardowns in this same lane were drafted, marked ready to post, and then closed with no outcome ever recorded — the identical failure mode is available to this batch. Nothing here has been tested against how a named brand would actually receive an unsolicited teardown of itself.
teardown-1-fresh.operator_read: The proof assets exist and they're good; this shelf has held good ones before.

video-studio-edit-bay.lede: The studio is built and its taste layer is in place, but nothing has been run through it end to end. Its own handoff lists the pilots as unrun and several dependencies as cloned but unwired.
video-studio-edit-bay.next_move: Run the first pilot through the studio and tell Farrice exactly what to record.

why.0: A pipeline that has never carried real work is an assumption, and the unwired pieces will only announce themselves as failures on the first genuine run.

video-studio-edit-bay.caveats: Untested integrations and a naive vertical reframe are known and unresolved. Readiness here is the builder's claim, not a result — and the cost behaviour of a real run is unverified.
video-studio-edit-bay.operator_read: Fully built, never used — the first pilot is the only thing that will tell you whether it works.

extract-forge.lede: The extraction line is the busiest thing on the board and keeps shipping usable expert systems, but a good share of them close below the bar they were aiming for. The current build carries no functional debt — only an optional quality promotion.
extract-forge.next_move: Give the blind recognition verdict, or drop the promotion and move on.

why.0: It is the only thing holding a finished extraction open, and it needs a felt verdict no automated pass can supply.

extract-forge.caveats: Scores here are self-reported by the same pass that produced the work — the run marked needs-improvement and the run marked keep were graded by the same hand. Nothing in the record shows whether any of these extractions has since been used for anything.
extract-forge.operator_read: Volume is high and quality is uneven; the open question is which of these anyone actually deploys.

angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.lede: The listening engine runs on its own cadence and reliably produces a daily angle plus finished, vault-filed content built off it. The pipeline works; what it produces has not been graded by anything outside the engine.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.next_move: Publish the vaulted posts and record how they actually performed.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.caveats: Every entry logged here proves the run happened, not that the angle landed. The engine also feeds its own living documents, so a weak angle can persist and compound without any signal from outside the loop.
angle-map-listening-engine-v4-1.operator_read: The engine is dependable; nobody has checked whether its output moves anyone.

01-listing-content.lede: The listing package went through several rebuilds against real rejections — first the hooks, then the whole voice — and landed on an approved version. It is finished work sitting one send away from the client.
01-listing-content.next_move: Send the approved recording pack to Jen and stop editing it.

why.0: The remaining item is explicitly optional polish, and treating it as work is what keeps a finished package from reaching the client.

01-listing-content.caveats: The approval is recorded on our side only — nothing here confirms Jen received the pack or filmed from it. Whether these hooks hold up on camera is entirely unmeasured.
01-listing-content.operator_read: Approved and finished; the only thing left is hitting send.

deep-research.lede: This is the research lane rather than a project of its own. Its recent work is a debunking verdict that saved a build from being started and a sourcing pass that handed another thread its methodology — both landed as decisions someone could act on.
deep-research.next_move: Route the next research question through this lane instead of answering it from memory.
deep-research.caveats: The stored resume line points at a client positioning packet unrelated to the most recent runs, so this thread's saved state is stale against what it actually did.
deep-research.operator_read: Research here comes back with a verdict rather than a summary — including 'build nothing'.

go.lede: This is where the cash-launch planning happened: demand research, an adversarial pass on the offer, a launch plan, and the profile going live. The planning finished; the selling it was supposed to trigger has not appeared in the record since.
go.next_move: Log real outreach against the launch plan, or park the thread.

why.0: A planning thread that stops moving quietly becomes a plan nobody is executing, and this one carries the offer the whole campaign depends on.

go.caveats: Nothing here records a send, a reply or a payment — the launch is verified as designed, not as run. Demand for the offer at its stated price remains unconfirmed by any buyer.
go.operator_read: Everything is planned; nothing in the record proves anyone was contacted.

proof-to-market.lede: The offer itself is settled — positioning, scope and the modules underneath it — and every mission raised against it is closed. Nothing in this window touched it.
proof-to-market.next_move: Take the offer to a buyer exactly as written instead of revising it again.
proof-to-market.caveats: Ready here means internally agreed, not market-tested: no buyer has priced, accepted or rejected this offer on the record. With no recent activity, the thread's state is as-last-left rather than as-of-now.
proof-to-market.operator_read: The offer is done being designed; it's waiting on someone to say yes or no to it.

writers-room.lede: This lane rebuilt the profile voice through repeated takes and left behind something durable — a ratcheted voice card and a recorded protocol for how the pen should work. It has been quiet longer than anything else on the board.
writers-room.next_move: Decide whether the profile copy is finished, or park the lane and carry the voice card forward without it.

why.0: This is the lane where the profile-copy spiral happened before; leaving it half-open invites another round of variants in place of a decision.

writers-room.caveats: The last recorded state is a set of competing treatments, not a chosen one — nothing here says which take is live. The voice work has outlasted the artifact it was made for.
writers-room.operator_read: The voice card is the real output; the profile copy itself never got a final verdict.

system-audit.lede: The harness lane has done real structural work — removing blocking gates, wiring per-model behaviour, and putting a judgment floor under the second harness. Its own outcome log flags that at least one major finding was never absorbed by anyone.
system-audit.next_move: Read the unabsorbed audit findings and either act on them or close them out.
system-audit.caveats: This thread's stored resume line describes client listing work rather than harness work, so its state marker points at the wrong thing. Several entries are also self-graded by the system auditing itself, which is the weakest available reviewer for a claim that the system improved.
system-audit.operator_read: Good structural fixes shipped; the audits themselves keep going unread.
